GAUTENG BABY OVERCROWDING: Too many babies in one cot

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Over crowding in maternity wards are putting lives of new borns at risk

Summary:
Over 2000 babies dies in gauteng in 2019 from alleged negligence

Over crowding in state maternity units is putting both the lives of newborns risk. Due to the close proximity of cots and unhygienic conditions there have recurring outbreaks of the CRE virus in neonatal units in Gauteng namely at Thembisa, Rahima Moosa and Thelle Mogoerane Hospital.

Case studies
Tapelo gave birth to her second child, this was the girl they had been praying for but she passed away after three days in NICU from the CRE virus due to over crowding at Thembisa
Lesego gave birth to twins at Thembisa in November 2019, after a week one of them died from CRE. Her other daughter is still in quarantine fighting for her life.
A second mother lost her only child in October after it was in NICU for two weeks. Also due to overcrowding, which lead to her getting a respiratory infection.
Tapelo's son was so strong when he was born all he had was some yellow Jaundice, but he never come back from NICU. He died of CRE at Thembisa in December 2019

Thembisa has give us access to film at the hospital. The CEO, head matron and nurse at NICU have agreed to speak to us about the dire situation at the ward. They say they tried to warn government and tried to beg them to do something, but nothing is changing so people must see what the conditions are that they are working in.

They have beds for 50 patients, but on average they have 91 women in the maternity ward. Their Neonatal ICU has space for 5 cots on the day we visited there were over 11 babies in there with their moms trying to feed them.



Further information:
Footage and stories from other hospitals
Bara and Tambo memorial - We have footage from the nurses inside
Both nurses will speak anonymously

Press Release:


Gauteng’s Maternity Ward Crisis: Baby Overcrowding
For two months late last year, the deadly antibiotic resistant CRE (Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae), ravaged the maternity ward of Tembisa Hospital in Gauteng, killing ten babies. But this wasn’t the first time that a number of infants have died in the same period inside a public health facility. Notorious for being overcrowded and understaffed, Carte Blanche investigates whether congestion in state hospitals could be putting the lives of new-born babies at risk.
Producer: Tarryn Crossman | Research: Nhlanhla Hlongwane | Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:

























Time code Character/
Visual
00:00:00 Nurse We are supposed to have 40 on the 2nd of December we are having 100 babies inside the ward.
2 00:00:10 Claire and Nurse Claire: How many people must one nurse look after?

One is to 20

3 00:00:16 VO Overcrowding in hospitals across Gauteng has been escalating for years. Our Maternity wards are breaking under the burden. Nurses say mother and baby wards at Thembisa are almost 80% overcrowded at any given
time, Which was a contributing factor to their recent outbreak CRE infections
4 00:00:37 Claire In November last year Tembisa hospital had. An outbreak of antibiotic resistance CRE infections in 2 months 10. Babies died

5 00:00:46 VO There have been three outbreaks of CRE infections in three different Gauteng hospitals over
the past two years resulting in the death of 19 babies
The Human Rights Commission attributed some of the outbreaks to overcrowding, unhygienic wards and inadequate infrastructure. Even though the outbreak at Thembisa Hospital is over, during our visit 11 babies,
still carrying the CRE infection, were being isolated in a separate ward. Nurse Mdanisi Ramela took us around the neonatal ICU
6 00:01:17 Nurse Mdanisi The beds we are supposed to be having here is 14 there are time where we go up to 30. According to. IPC protocol the babies are supposed to be 1 meter apart. Which is difficult we cant, structurally we cant and we are the only hospital around here

This is our prem extension its where we are supposed to be having 4 babies. We are. Having 10 at the moment.
7 00:01:42 VO GAUTENG HEALTH MEC Bandile Masuku acknowledges that overcrowding in maternity wards is a problem across Gauteng
8 00:01:48 MEC and Claire MEC: The issue of overcrowding in maternity in maternity is an issue of. The numbers. We are talking about 15,2 million officially but we do have patterns. Of migrations that happen that see us going to closer to 17 million. It is a situation like Tembisa, most of the women who come to hospitals are. Not necessarily supposed to deliver in hospital they are supposed to deliver in clinics because they are low risk patients. And the last one that we do have a lot of immigration from other countries.

9 00:02:21 V/O The situation at Rahima Moosa Mother and Child Hospital, is no better. This video filmed by a patient at Rahima Moosa in 2019 it shows a woman in Labour on the floor of the hospital with with no nurses available to assist her. Blessing, which is not his real name, has been working as a nurse at the maternity ward at Rahima Moosa for over 2 years.
10 00:02:49 Blessing That hospital is very. Crowded in the pits in the maternity, everywhere its just over. Crowded. In the ANC the ward where they admit mothers who have got problems. There are supposed to have 41 but they always have extra 12 or 15 mothers sitting, just sitting on the bench.

11 00:03:08 Voice over Veaan crawford was only 30 weeks pregnant when her water broke making her a high risk patient, she was therefore referred to Rahima Moosa
12 00:03:17 Veaan I got to Rahima Moosa at 11:30 in the morning. So now its one big room crowded full of. Women and there is not enough beds it was every where there are chairs everywhere so around 10pm at night a doctor came so I got. Up because I was soaking wet now because the fluid is leaking so he did a few test and left for like. 15 mintues and came back and said okay your water definitely broke. Just go back to. Seat and we have access other people and we will let you know when there. Is an available bed.

13 00:03:47 VO Veaan’s water broke 10 weeks prematurely and according to treatment guidelines she should have received antibiotics within 24 hours – and mother and baby should have been closely monitored.
14 00:04:03 V/O The day we arrived at Thembisa Hospital, 15 women in various stages of labour were waiting to be admitted, but only 4 beds available and 2 midwives were
available. Nurse Rapanyane MOKGADI is the head nurse in this ward.
15 00:04:17 Rapanyane We are dealing with a lot and its stressful, we are. Like this throughout the day. We want to help, we want to give them the best, we want to but there is no time.
16 00:04:27 VO It was not only the admissions ward that was overcrowded, the theatre was completely backed up, as there was only one doctor on duty. Patients that were in obvious pain were told to wait on a bench until a spot in theatre opened up. Meanwhile, the list of emergency caesarean section deliveries just kept getting longer.
17 00:04:43 So this list, all these patients are emergencies and all these patients have got to prioritise those ones that are. More urgent. All of them, they are serious cases so which one do you take out of this?

18 00:04:56 V/O Nurse Matjatji Phasha is the operations manager in Labour ward 13 at Tembisa. We were asked not to film in this ward to protect the identities of the mothers. But According to the staff at Tembisa these photos taken of the ward in 2019 are still an accurate reflection
19 00:05:11 Matjatji We are unable to give the care that we need to give, we know that we are failing. There’s a risk to unborn baby that we need to monitor. The monitoring with the machines should be about 4 – 6 hourly and if we are missing those 2 timelines and then you go. And check and then you don’t find a thing and you have lost the baby
20 00:05:34 BV/O According to Veaan not Once in the four days that she waited on a bench did anyone check her babies heart rate. It was Only once she was admitted that they picked up that her baby was in distress and she was immediately induced, soon going into active labour

21 00:05:50 VEAAN I could feel my son pushing and pushing. And there were 3 other women in the same room and so when I opened my legs my son was half out and I was screaming “somebody help, can somebody help the baby is coming” and a nurse. Came in and said “what now?” and she runs out and. Runs for hand gloves and a sheet and she comes. Back and she say the baby is coming and like okay. Just lay back and push. So I gave one push and its out.

22 00:06:18 VO Veaan’s son was sent to neo-natal ICU at Rahima Moosa. He weighed only 1.4kg. Veaan says she saw his condition deteriorate in ICU. She felt he was neglected.
23 00:06:33 VEAAN So the next day I came in and I’m like whats wrong with my son and they were like no this is just to monitor your baby so im like. “is there anything wrong with my son?” they like “NO” so we do our normal visits and a nurse comes and she’s like okay. This is what happened “your son had bleeding to the lungs” it didn’t affect his brain hes okay. We just let him sleep. The bleeding to the lungs stopped. I feel like I wasn’t told the truth when I go today “your son had bleeding to the lungs” and when I go the next day “ oh no your son is fine”

24 00:07:02 VO According to Nurse Blessing because there are too many babies in the neonatal ICU at Rahima Moosa and there are not enough vital sign monitors to ensure the safety of every baby in the ward.

Veaan says 12 hours passed, after her son took a turn for the worst, before the hospital staff called her in.
28 00:07:15 BLESSING At other hospitals the vital. Signs are monitored continuously because the conditions could change anytime. Each and every. Baby has got their own monitor at Rahima Moosa now we have got 2 machines on the walls with 18 babies and sometimes you could have 20 babies there so we. Check vital signs only every 3 hours
29 00:07:41 Veaan So we got to the hospital on the 25th around 8:30 in the morning and I go straight to my baby. And hes blue, and now my son is on multiple machines, multiple pipes but you can see his body is blue. “no what happened was your. Baby took a bad turn the previous. Night, your baby stopped breathing for one sec and no oxygen went to his brain and now hes brain dead” sorry… and so the doctor was like “ look we have to out the machines off, theres nothing we can do for your son” and he said to me the doctors saying the cause of his. Death is sleep apnea

30 00:08:33 Blessing Vital signs are monitor can detect sleep apnea so.. yeah we could’ve monitoresd if we had enough machines

31 00:08:42 Claire and MEC CLAIRE: COULD YOU SAY THAT the current over crowding is having any effect. On our neonatal mortality rate

MEC: It does, its one of the factors.

32 00:08:52 Blessing The hospital administration they are aware of what is happening in the hospital. Sometimes when you tell them we are over crowded and we need staff. To come and work and then he said goodluck

33 00:09:07 MEC: Rahima moosa also has a big problem of leadership, its one of the hospitals that have not had. A CEO for the past 4 years

34 00:09:16 VO MEC Masuku HAD undertook to have all 14 CEO vacancies at Gauteng hospitals filled by the end 2019. However, three are still open, which he says will be rectified by the end of March..
35 00:09:29 MEC For hospitals like Tembisa its to get extra space for them somewhere. So we are creating what we are going to call Siezer hubs – long term build more facilities

Claire: have we taken too long to react to the over crowding?

Mec: I would say yes, people plan and then have a meeting to discuss the plan and then have a meeting to fund the plan. It becomes a problem so I don’t want to be in that cycle

36 00:09:54 Nurse Mandi Let me tell you, with the. What we have we are doing so good, few people can survive in this situation

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Over crowding in maternity wards are putting lives of new borns at risk
metadata.Summary: Over 2000 babies dies in gauteng in 2019 from alleged negligence Over crowding in state maternity units is putting both the lives of newborns risk. Due to the close proximity of cots and unhygienic conditions there have recurring outbreaks of the CRE virus in neonatal units in Gauteng namely at Thembisa, Rahima Moosa and Thelle Mogoerane Hospital. Case studies Tapelo gave birth to her second child, this was the girl they had been praying for but she passed away after three days in NICU from the CRE virus due to over crowding at Thembisa Lesego gave birth to twins at Thembisa in November 2019, after a week one of them died from CRE. Her other daughter is still in quarantine fighting for her life. A second mother lost her only child in October after it was in NICU for two weeks. Also due to overcrowding, which lead to her getting a respiratory infection. Tapelo's son was so strong when he was born all he had was some yellow Jaundice, but he never come back from NICU. He died of CRE at Thembisa in December 2019 Thembisa has give us access to film at the hospital. The CEO, head matron and nurse at NICU have agreed to speak to us about the dire situation at the ward. They say they tried to warn government and tried to beg them to do something, but nothing is changing so people must see what the conditions are that they are working in. They have beds for 50 patients, but on average they have 91 women in the maternity ward. Their Neonatal ICU has space for 5 cots on the day we visited there were over 11 babies in there with their moms trying to feed them.
